title: Phase 1: extract sqlator-service shared application layer
description:
Extract the application logic duplicated between src-tauri/src/commands.rs and web-server/src/handlers.rs into a new sqlator-service crate sitting between sqlator-core and the frontends.

Named sqlator-service, not sqlator-app, because the src-tauri package is already named sqlator-app.

Eight modules: connections, connect, ssh, docker, credentials, schema, portability, terminal_spec.

Migrate Tauri first (smaller diff - it has the more complete orchestration behavior), then web, then the TUI. That is a sequencing choice, NOT a rule that Tauri's implementation wins every divergence: winners are chosen per ledger row.

Also fixes two blocking-call hazards that would freeze a GTK frame: ConfigManager's synchronous file I/O behind non-async signatures, and VaultBackend::unlock running Argon2id at 19 MiB / 2 iterations. Both need spawn_blocking. And makes connections.json writes atomic and internally synchronized.

## Context
Open design decisions that must be answered during the phase: tunnel registry key collision (connect_database keys by connection id, create_ssh_tunnel by profile id); error typing (SshError/DockerError have no conversion into CoreError); export path policy; web's single_db mode.
acceptance_criteria: sqlator-service exists as a workspace member with the eight modules; commands.rs and handlers.rs each drop below ~400 lines and contain only glue; the third copy of credential resolution (terminal.rs:364) is gone; divergences 1-4 fixed; exactly one table-extraction fallback exists and it is plan 007's corrected version; TUI can open an SSH-tunneled and a Docker connection; Svelte frontend runs unchanged against both Tauri and web
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: sqlator-service extracted; Tauri/web/TUI on AppService; divergences 1-4 addressed via shared connect/SSH/docker/portability; single extract_table_regex from plan 007.

title: GTK4/libadwaita native frontend
description:
Add a native GNOME frontend to SQLator as a fourth frontend, and extract the shared service layer it needs.

SQLator has four frontends' worth of ambition and one frontend's worth of shared code. Roughly 1,000-1,100 of the 1,727 lines in src-tauri/src/commands.rs have a near-verbatim twin in web-server/src/handlers.rs, and the two copies have drifted into five user-visible bugs. tui-app avoided the duplication by depending only on sqlator-core, and consequently cannot use SSH tunnels, Docker connections, or the credential store at all.

A fourth frontend must pick one of those two failure modes unless the service layer is extracted first. So extraction comes first and the GTK app becomes its first consumer.

Five phases: 0a/0b (prerequisites, parallel), 1 (service extraction), 2 (GTK skeleton), 3 (parity), 4 (packaging). Plus a cross-cutting testing/tooling plan that is not a phase.

title: refactor: shared SSH session with multiple local forwards
description:
## Why
Phase 1d keys the tunnel registry by (ssh_profile_id, target_host, target_port) because TunnelHandle is 1:1 with a single local forward. Same bastion + different DB targets therefore open duplicate SSH sessions.

## What
Lift session↔forward coupling in sqlator-core and sqlator-service so one authenticated session per SSH profile can own many LocalForward listeners. Refcount forwards, then the session.

## Acceptance
- Two connections, same profile, different targets → one SSH handshake, two local ports
- Dropping one forward leaves the other working; dropping the last tears down the session
- Ephemeral test_* teardown still never leaks a listener/session
- Design base: docs/plans/gtk/2026-07-26-001-design-ssh-tunnel-registry-keying.md
acceptance_criteria: One SSH session per profile can host multiple local forwards; refcount teardown; characterization/ephemeral teardown preserved

title: fix: correct table extraction and editability verdict in both frontends
description:
extract_table_regex exists in both src-tauri/src/commands.rs:1584 and web-server/src/handlers.rs:1133, and BOTH copies are wrong, in different directions.

Verified empirically in a scratch crate:
1. Tauri rejects any comma anywhere, so 'SELECT a, b FROM t' returns None - a plain false negative.
2. Web returns Some(("t1", None)) for 'SELECT a, b FROM t1 , t2', treating an implicit cross join as editable. That is a data-safety hole Tauri blocks only by accident.
3. Tauri's sequential .trim_matches('"').trim_matches('`') leaves stray quotes on a backtick-quoted quoted identifier; web's single-predicate pass returns the bare name.
4. Present in BOTH copies and captured by no divergence row: from_idx is computed on sql.to_uppercase() and then used to slice sql. to_uppercase() is not length-preserving, so "SELECT 'iii' FROM t" (with dotless i) extracts the table name "OM".

Fix is web's permissiveness on the SELECT list combined with Tauri's strictness on the FROM clause: delimit the FROM region first, then check for commas and JOIN only inside it. And index against the original string.

Impact is latent rather than live: of 28 dialect-specific constructs tested against GenericDialect (sqlparser 0.54 in both crates), only the mysql CLI \G failed to parse, so the regex fallback rarely fires. Note that switching to dialect-specific parsers would REDUCE coverage - PostgreSqlDialect rejects MySQL backticks.

## Context
Supersedes divergence ledger rows 5-7 of phase 0a. Soft relationship with phase 1 in either order: if this lands first, phase 1 moves one corrected function; if phase 1 lands first, it moves both copies as-is and this fixes the merged one.
acceptance_criteria: One implementation, correct on all four bugs above; test corpus covers comma-in-select-list, implicit comma join, mixed quoting, and the non-length-preserving uppercase case; both frontends give the same editability verdict
close_reason: Fixed extract_table_regex in both frontends: FROM-region comma/JOIN check, ASCII case-insensitive FROM scan, single-pass unquoting, MSSQL brackets, quoted-dot split, \G token stop. Fallback editability reason distinguished from multi-table.

title: Phase 2: sqlator-gtk crate and application skeleton
description:
Stand up the sqlator-gtk crate (in the gtk/ directory, added to workspace.members): build pipeline, tokio/GLib bridge, application shell, action and accelerator map.

Deliverable is an app that launches, remembers its window state, and can run a query end to end.

Cargo-only build for this phase - meson and Flatpak arrive in phase 4, written fresh. Blueprint is compiled via build.rs, NOT the gtk4/blueprint cargo feature (that feature does not support resource=).

Pinned crates matching the verified local environment: gtk4 0.11.4 (gnome_50), libadwaita 0.9.2 (v1_9, gtk_v4_22), sourceview5 0.11.2 (v5_18 is the feature ceiling - there is no v5_20), vte4 0.10.0 (v0_84, optional and feature-gated, Linux/BSD only).

## Context
gio::Settings::new() aborts the process if the schema is not installed. build.rs must compile the gschema into OUT_DIR/schemas and main() must set GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR before constructing any Settings.
